label: geodetic latitude
definition: The latitude on maps and from GPS, defined by the normal to the reference ellipsoid. It differs from geocentric latitude by up to 11.5 arcminutes near 45 degrees.

label: geocentric latitude
definition: The angle between the equatorial plane and the line from the Earth's centre to the observer. Eclipse formulas use it, through $\rho\sin\phi'$ and $\rho\cos\phi'$, to place the observer in the fundamental plane.

label: reference ellipsoid
definition: The oblate spheroid that stands in for the Earth's shape in geodesy and in eclipse computation, defined by an equatorial radius and a flattening (for example WGS 84 or the IAU 1976 figure).

label: geoid
definition: The equipotential surface of the Earth's gravity field that mean sea level would follow. It lies between 106 m below and 85 m above the WGS 84 ellipsoid.

label: orthometric height
definition: Height above the geoid, which is what "elevation above sea level" and most digital elevation models give.

label: ellipsoidal height
definition: Height above the reference ellipsoid, which is what GPS receivers measure natively and what the eclipse formulas need when the observer is placed on the ellipsoid plus a height.

label: UT1
definition: Universal Time proper, a measure of the Earth's rotation angle. Eclipse predictions labelled "UT" are in UT1, obtained from TT by subtracting ΔT.

label: UTC
definition: Coordinated Universal Time, the atomic civil time scale kept within 0.9 s of UT1 by leap seconds. TAI − UTC has been 37 s since 2017 January 1.

label: TAI
definition: International Atomic Time, the continuous atomic time scale from which TT (TAI + 32.184 s) and UTC (TAI minus an integer number of leap seconds) are derived.

label: leap second
definition: A one-second step inserted into UTC to keep it within 0.9 s of UT1. The accumulated offset between TAI and UTC has been 37 s since 2017.

label: DUT1
definition: The value of UT1 − UTC broadcast with time signals, rounded to 0.1 s. It is the correction needed to turn UT1 contact times into UTC.

label: length of day (lod)
definition: The duration of the mean solar day measured in SI seconds, minus 86400 s. Its slow growth, about 1.8 ms per century on average, is what makes ΔT increase roughly parabolically.

label: polar motion
definition: The wandering of the Earth's rotation axis relative to the crust, a few tenths of an arcsecond, which displaces an observer's position relative to the axis by up to about 10 m.

label: Greenwich apparent sidereal time (GAST)
definition: The hour angle of the true equinox of date at Greenwich. The Besselian element μ is GAST minus the right ascension of the shadow axis, evaluated at the UT1 of the instant.

label: equation of the equinoxes
definition: The difference between apparent and mean sidereal time caused by nutation, at most about 1.1 s of time.

label: nutation
definition: The short-period wobble of the Earth's axis superposed on precession, modelled by the IAU 1980 or IAU 2000A series. It moves the equinox by up to about 17 arcseconds.

label: precession
definition: The slow drift of the Earth's rotation axis and equinox, about 50 arcseconds per year, which fixes the equator and equinox of date to which Besselian elements are referred.

label: atmospheric refraction
definition: The bending of light in the atmosphere that lifts the apparent altitude of a body, by about 34 arcminutes on the horizon, 10 arcminutes at 5 degrees and 1 arcminute at 45 degrees.

label: elevation factor
definition: Espenak's multiplier $\tan(90^{\circ} - A)\sin D$, where $A$ is the Sun's altitude and $D$ the difference between the Sun's azimuth and the path-limit azimuth, giving the perpendicular shift of the path limit per unit of observer elevation.

label: tan f₁, tan f₂
definition: The tangents of the half-angles of the penumbral ($f_1$) and umbral ($f_2$) shadow cones, about 0.00467 and 0.00465. They convert an observer's height above the fundamental plane into a change of shadow radius.

label: μ (Greenwich hour angle of the shadow axis)
definition: The Besselian element that ties the shadow to the rotating Earth. It is ephemeris sidereal time minus the right ascension of the shadow axis, so it is the element through which ΔT enters.

label: SPICE binary PCK (bpc) Earth orientation kernel
definition: A NAIF file of Earth orientation (precession, nutation, UT1 and polar motion) used by SVS to orient the Earth. The "predict" kernels extrapolate the IERS series into the future.
